main_wing_spar.name: Tapered I-Beam Main Spar
main_wing_spar.model: Timoshenko beam FEA, 2 DOF/node, 21 sizing stations + Saint-Venant root-warping stress recovery
assumptions: Same solver and stations as the contract FeaResult; optimisation scales t_f and t_w linearly root→tip
Gauges clamped to Raymer minimums t_f ≥ 2.0 mm, t_w ≥ 1.5 mm
Mass is one semi-span of spar (multiply by 2 for both wings)
main_wing_spar.convergence_note: Stations fixed by the spar sizing (21 nodes).

metrics.governing: outer cap fibre at y = 0.91 m

ai_proposal.rationale: Baseline margin is 0.1107, governed by the outer cap fibre at y = 0.91 m under spanwise bending. A slight root gauge reduction to 0.99 trims mass while keeping the peak cap bending stress safely above the 0.10 margin floor.

verified_metrics.governing: outer cap fibre at y = 0.91 m

ai_proposal.verdict: accepted: solver confirms the constraint and a near-optimal objective

ai_proposal.rationale: Wait-free mass redistribution from the lightly loaded tip toward the root cap and web reduces peak bending stress across the inboard stations while keeping total spar mass below baseline.

ai_proposal.rationale: Minimising tip gauge to 0.60 frees mass budget to thicken the root cap and web to 1.21, directly lowering the root bending and warping von Mises stress within the 1.05x mass limit.

wing_skin_box.name: NACA 2415 Wing Torsion Box
wing_skin_box.model: NACA 2415 single-cell thin-wall box: Timoshenko bending + Bredt-Batho torsion, 25 nodes
assumptions: Skin carries the full ultimate wing bending (spar caps excluded: conservative, no stringers)
Torque t(y) = q·c·(0.10 − 0.05/1.2): lift at c/4, box reference at 0.35c, c_m0 = −0.05 at c_l ≈ 1.2
Spar webs at 15% and 60% chord; 10 ribs per side, 0.8 mm, 50% lightening holes
Uniform-gauge baseline from a first-pass hand sizing to margin +0.25; skin buckling not checked
wing_skin_box.convergence_note: Peak σ_vM re-solved at three node counts.

metrics.governing: skin (bending + Bredt torsion) at y = 0.00 m

ai_proposal.rationale: With a 0.25 baseline margin governed at the y = 0.00 m root skin under combined bending and Bredt-Batho torsion, reducing root gauge to 0.90 and tapering tip gauge to 0.65 cuts mass while holding margin above 0.10.

verified_metrics.governing: skin (bending + Bredt torsion) at y = 0.00 m

ai_proposal.verdict: rejected: feasible but more than 2% worse than the solver grid optimum (182.90 kg vs 178.04 kg)

metrics.governing: skin (bending + Bredt torsion) at y = 0.00 m
skin (bending + Bredt torsion) at y = 0.00 m

min_mass.rationale: Grid search over 169 solver runs; lightest gauge set holding margin ≥ +0.10. Root skin & web gauge ×0.90, tip skin & web gauge ×0.60: mass -51.42 kg, peak σ_vM 270 → 300 MPa, margin +0.25 → +0.12. Governing: skin (bending + Bredt torsion) at y = 0.00 m.

ai_proposal.rationale: Stress drops rapidly outboard along the torsion box, so reducing tip skin gauge to 0.60 allows a 1.20 root gauge increase at constant mass, substantially boosting the root bending-torsion margin.

verified_metrics.governing: skin (bending + Bredt torsion) at y = 0.00 m

ai_proposal.verdict: rejected: feasible but more than 2% worse than the solver grid optimum (margin +0.50 vs margin +0.62)

max_margin.rationale: Grid search over 169 solver runs; highest margin at no added mass (material moved toward the governing zone). Root skin & web gauge ×1.30, tip skin & web gauge ×0.60: mass -1.24 kg, peak σ_vM 270 → 208 MPa, margin +0.25 → +0.62. Governing: skin (bending + Bredt torsion) at y = 0.00 m.

ai_proposal.rationale: Setting tip gauge to the 0.60 floor and using the 5% mass allowance permits a 1.30 root skin and web gauge, maximally reducing root combined bending and Bredt shear stress.

horizontal_tail.name: Horizontal Tail NACA 0012 Box
horizontal_tail.model: NACA 0012 single-cell thin-wall box: Timoshenko bending + Bredt-Batho torsion, 21 nodes
assumptions: Tail semi-span 0.357 × wing semi-span and root chord 0.65 × wing root chord (GA ratios, assumed)
Ultimate tail load 0.12 × MTOW·g·n_ult, elliptic spanwise (assumed balance + manoeuvre load)
Torque from load at c/4 about the 0.35c box reference; webs at 12% and 65% chord
Uniform-gauge baseline from a first-pass hand sizing to margin +0.25; skin buckling not checked
horizontal_tail.convergence_note: Peak σ_vM re-solved at three node counts.

fuselage_frames.name: Wing Carry-Through Ring Frames & Bridge
fuselage_frames.model: Closed-ring force method (2 redundants, 721 points/half ring) + carry-through beam
assumptions: Fuselage radius 0.89 m scaled from a 1.22 m GA cabin by MTOW^(1/3) (assumed)
Wing root shear split 70% main / 15% front / 15% rear frame; reacted by skin shear q = 2V·sinφ/(πR)
Bridge = spar root I-section carrying the full root moment across the cabin
Frames are 65 mm deep I-sections; uniform-gauge baseline from hand sizing to margin +0.25
fuselage_frames.convergence_note: Frame peak (excluding the bridge) vs ring integration points per half ring.

metrics.governing: carry-through bridge cap (root moment)

ai_proposal.rationale: The carry-through bridge cap governs at a tight 0.1025 baseline margin under root bending moment, whereas the front and rear frames peak at 198 MPa; maintaining k_root at 1.00 and reducing k_tip to 0.65 cuts frame mass without violating the 0.10 margin.
ai_proposal.verdict: accepted: solver confirms the constraint and a near-optimal objective

metrics.governing: carry-through bridge cap (root moment)
carry-through bridge cap (root moment)

min_mass.rationale: The carry-through bridge cap governs at a tight 0.1025 baseline margin under root bending moment, whereas the front and rear frames peak at 198 MPa; maintaining k_root at 1.00 and reducing k_tip to 0.65 cuts frame mass without violating the 0.10 margin.

ai_proposal.rationale: Reducing the under-stressed front and rear ring frames to 0.65 frees mass to thicken the main frame and carry-through bridge cap to 1.25, directly increasing the governing root moment margin at neutral mass.
ai_proposal.verdict: rejected by solver: margin +0.34, mass 60.44 kg breaks the goal constraint

metrics.governing: carry-through bridge cap (root moment)

ai_proposal.rationale: Dropping front and rear frame gauges to 0.60 and using the 5% mass allowance enables a 1.35 gauge on the main frame and carry-through bridge, substantially lowering root cap bending stress.
ai_proposal.verdict: rejected by solver: margin +0.43, mass 63.94 kg breaks the goal constraint

main_landing_gear.name: Cantilever Tubular Main Gear Strut
main_landing_gear.model: Curved cantilever tube: 3D small-rotation curvature integration (bending + Saint-Venant torsion), 33 nodes
assumptions: Landing load factor 3.0 limit × 1.5 ultimate, 90% of MTOW on the mains (assumed, FAR 23.473 style)
Spin-up drag 0.25 × vertical reaction applied at the axle; side load not modelled
Spec material (al_2024_t3) used for the strut: steel is not in the verified material table
Tube OD 120 → 86 mm; uniform wall baseline from hand sizing to margin +0.25
sources: Megson 6ed Ch. 16-18 (bending, torsion of closed tubes)
main_landing_gear.convergence_note: Peak σ_vM re-solved at three node counts.

metrics.governing: tube wall at s = 0.00 m (bending + torsion)

ai_proposal.rationale: The cantilever strut has a negative baseline margin (-0.2213) governed by combined bending and Saint-Venant torsion at the s = 0.00 m hip attach wall; increasing hip gauge to 1.55 restores the required 0.10 margin with minimal added mass.

ai_proposal.verdict: rejected by solver: margin -0.22, mass 18.92 kg breaks the goal constraint

ai_proposal.rationale: Because bending and torsional moments decay toward the axle, tapering the axle-end wall to 0.60 allows the governing hip wall gauge to increase to 1.28 within the baseline mass budget.

engine_mount.name: Engine Mount Spaceframe Truss
engine_mount.model: Pin-jointed 3D spaceframe: direct stiffness (24 DOF, 14 bars) + Euler buckling per member
assumptions: Engine + propeller mass 0.11 × MTOW at 0.30 m ahead of the ring, inertia n_ult·m·g (assumed)
Ultimate thrust 1.5 × 0.25 × MTOW·g; propeller torque and gyroscopic loads not modelled
Firewall hard points pinned; members pinned-pinned (K = 1) for buckling
Zone factor k scales tube OD and wall by √k (constant D/t); baseline hand-sized to margin +0.25
engine_mount.convergence_note: Exact for a pin-jointed truss (one bar element per member).

metrics.governing: member D4 (buckling)

ai_proposal.rationale: With a 0.25 baseline margin governed by Euler buckling in diagonal member D4 and peak longeron stress at 216 MPa, scaling both tube zones down to 0.90 reduces spaceframe mass while keeping buckling and axial margins above 0.10.
ai_proposal.verdict: rejected by solver: margin +0.01, mass 1.76 kg breaks the goal constraint

metrics.governing: member L3 (buckling)
member L3 (buckling)

min_mass.rationale: Grid search over 169 solver runs; lightest gauge set holding margin ≥ +0.10. Longeron tubes ×0.90, diagonal & ring tubes ×1.00: mass -0.06 kg, peak σ_vM 216 → 240 MPa, margin +0.25 → +0.21. Governing: member L3 (buckling).

ai_proposal.rationale: Euler buckling in diagonal D4 governs the baseline 0.25 margin while the root longerons have greater headroom, so shifting mass from longerons (0.95) to diagonal and ring tubes (1.05) raises the governing buckling margin at constant mass.
ai_proposal.verdict: rejected by solver: margin +0.35, mass 1.99 kg breaks the goal constraint

ai_proposal.rationale: Trimming the diagonal and ring tube gauge to 0.85 while maintaining positive D4 buckling margin frees mass to boost the longeron tubes to 1.30, substantially reducing peak axial stress in the root longerons.
